card.name: Punctuation and links before a named condition
card.fires_on: Commas, small linking words and spaces that sit just before a medical condition or adverse effect is named, such as acidosis, hypoglycemia or respiratory depression. It appears in side-effect and overdose text.

modes.label: Comma before acidosis
modes.description: A comma after 'non-anion gap' just before 'hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis'.
modes.example: induce non-anion gap<<,>> hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis

modes.label: Link before hypoglycemia
modes.description: A verb or preposition in overdose text that leads into 'hypoglycemia'.
modes.example: an overdose of miglitol tablets will not result<< in>> hypoglycemia.

modes.label: List opener for effects
modes.description: Punctuation after 'e.g' that opens a list of toxic effects.
